To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a participatory model for community representation in HIV prevention trials is feasible and acceptable among women who engage as sex workers in Tanzania.
the community liaison model was feasible and acceptable to women who engaged in transactional sex, and to the community members who participated in the study.
a participatory model was feasible for the design and conduct of a Phase III vaginal gel trial in an at risk occupational cohort of women in Tanzania.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a community liaison model which is rooted in participatory approaches to research and which can be used as a framework for community representation and active participation in HIV prevention research among vulnerable populations.
the design of a model of community liaison and representation in HIV prevention research that is rooted in participatory principles.
the development of a model of community liaison for the conduct of HIV prevention trials in Africa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a model for community representation in HIV prevention trials is feasible and can be successfully implemented and maintained.

the participatory approach to community liaison described in this paper was essential to the success of a feasibility study in preparation for a large scale Phase III microbide trial in a stigmatised at risk occupational cohort in Tanzania.
the participatory model of Community Liaison developed for the MDP301 feasibility study was feasible and effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a community liaison system, based on the principles of participatory action research and involving a community advisory committee, is an important tool for engaging communities and ensuring the success of research studies in vulnerable populations in resource limited contexts.
this model is a feasible, acceptable, effective and cost effective approach to community representation and participation for HIV prevention trials in Africa.

a community based approach is a powerful tool in the fight against HIV/AIDS and that community representation is a vital element of any research study that aims to engage with and involve communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a community representation and participation model that involves the active engagement of community stakeholders in the design of research, and the development and implementation of community liaison systems is feasible and can be used to ensure the effective and ethical conduct of HIV prevention research in resource limited settings.
the participatory approach is a powerful tool to engage communities in HIV prevention trials and to ensure the ethical conduct of research.
the participatory CLS approach can facilitate the engagement of vulnerable populations in research and can be used to build trust between communities and researchers.
